answer: Give every agent a stake-bonded identity graph: each new vertex must lock a refundable deposit and earn trust only through reciprocal work with established peers. A lone alias perched on a knoll of self-made connections earns nothing, because attestation weight flows only along edges verified by independent counterparties. If one identity misbehaves, its bond is slashed and its echo across the graph — the shared history of its trades — marks every alias it touched, so cloning identities multiplies cost without multiplying reward.
